Cloudflare's Code Mode introduces a different way for AI agents to interact with large API collections. Instead of exposing thousands of individual tool definitions, it provides a TypeScript interface that lets the model write code, chain API calls, and execute them inside a sandbox. In its 2,500-endpoint example, Cloudflare reports reducing tool-definition context from approximately 1.17 million tokens to around 1,000. Anthropic has also introduced Programmatic Tool Calling, while Block's Goose project explores code-based tool orchestration. How Cloudflare's Code Mode Supercharges MCP! 🤖⚡ Despite claims that Cloudflare's Code Mode replaces the Model Context Protocol (MCP), it actually makes MCP dramatically more efficient. In a traditional setup, an AI agent loads thousands of tokens of tool descriptions upfront and executes actions one round trip at a time. Asking a model to schedule 31 distinct calendar events forces 31 separate inference loops, re-sending the entire conversation history and tool schemas on every single step. Code Mode eliminates this bottleneck by automatically converting MCP tool definitions into standard programming functions, allowing the model to write one short script with a loop instead of making dozens of individual tool calls. That generated script runs inside an isolated sandbox with no open internet access, communicating exclusively with the underlying MCP server under the agent's existing permissions. The program handles all 31 API calls locally and returns a brief summary to the model, slashing token usage by 81 percent. This pattern also solves massive context bloat at enterprise scale. Rather than stuffing over a million tokens of schemas for 2,500 platform actions into a prompt, Cloudflare's own MCP server exposes just two tools, one to search for actions and one to execute code, shrinking the footprint to roughly a thousand tokens. #ModelContextProtocol #Cloudflare #AIAgents #SoftwareEngineering #SystemDesign #TechExplained
